assigned.title: The automated half of the Windows matrix, running on Windows
assigned.acceptance: Every row PW-0601 marks automated runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails. REQUIRED: the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu -- the desktop axis is currently built on Ubuntu only, and only incidentally, because the axis defaults on and openssl happens to be installed. REQUIRED: the shell is driven end to end where the harness can reach it, and where it cannot, the row stays in the commander-machine half rather than being replaced by a unit test that proves something easier. REQUIRED: retries stay at zero, on the rule playwright.config.ts already states at length. REQUIRED: a row that is skipped says why, by name, the way the existing harness already does for the desktop and media-rig axes.

OWNERSHIP RESOLVED BY RESPONSIBILITY in round 87, on gpt-architect's ruling. .github/workflows/windows.yml moved from allowedPaths to reviewDependencies: this task is the certification CONSUMER -- it needs the workflow and the artifact to EXIST and to execute its rows, which is a read relationship. PW-0501 owns the workflow because PW-0501 produces the Windows artifact. A task does not co-own a production build workflow merely because its tests run there. If this task's acceptance genuinely requires editing that workflow after PW-0501 lands, it is sequenced AFTER PW-0501 -- its dependencies already say so -- and its narrowed write surface is derived from the actual change at claim time rather than reserved now. Neither task was narrowed to defeat conflictWithActive; the surfaces follow the implementation responsibility. ROUND 107 AMENDMENT, on gpt-architect's ruling: .github/workflows/windows.yml has MOVED from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths -- allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface, so leaving it in both is redundant and ai:validate says so. This is the condition the round-87 note above named -- PW-0501 has landed, and the acceptance clause 'runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails' cannot be satisfied without writing the only file that defines one. The surface was derived at claim time from the actual change, as that note required, and is the single file rather than .github/workflows/**. scripts/windows/** was deliberately NOT taken; it remains PW-0502's and PW-0503's. Conflict check and the cost to those two tasks' future fingerprints are recorded in the task.definition_changed event of this round.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck -- 22 tasks successful, 22 total (13.3s). RECORDED FOR COMPLETENESS AND WORTH READING AS SUCH: this round's change is .github/workflows/windows.yml only, which no TypeScript project compiles, so a pass here establishes that nothing ELSE was disturbed and nothing about the workflow. The evidence that bears on the change is in the e2e gate.

e2e.evidence:
WHAT THIS GATE ACTUALLY ESTABLISHES, STATED BEFORE THE NUMBERS, BECAUSE THE SUITE DOES NOT EXERCISE THE CHANGE. The round-107 change is .github/workflows/windows.yml only. Playwright does not read it. So: (a) 'npx playwright test --project=chromium --project=api' in development mode, 93 passed / 14 skipped in 1.9m, 0 failed -- no regression anywhere, which is all a Linux Playwright run can say about a Windows workflow; and (b) the evidence that DOES bear on the change, which is PowerShell, recorded here because this task has no gate named for it.

POWERSHELL EVIDENCE, EXECUTED NOT INSPECTED. PowerShell 7.4.6 was installed in this container (the windows-latest runner ships 7.4/7.5) and both added steps were extracted from the YAML by a parser rather than retyped.
  1. PARSE. [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile over all five pwsh steps in the file, including the three this round did not touch: 0 errors. A pwsh syntax error in the publisher step would fail the job, and the publisher deliberately carries no continue-on-error, so this was checked rather than assumed.
  2. EXECUTION, four branches, against reports built by calling the REAL scripts/windows/ modules -- loadPlan, readIdentity, locations, classifyResidue -- not by hand-writing JSON.
     - report present, all cases passing: renders the table, the outstanding list (F1 launch, F3 real-user-data, F5 SmartScreen, F6 update) and four collapsible JSON details. exit 0.
     - report absent: says NO REPORT WAS PRODUCED and explains that a refusal is a wiring fault in the workflow rather than a product failure. exit 0. An empty table that reads as a clean machine is the failure mode this branch exists to prevent.
     - a FAILING F3 whose scenario text contains a pipe and a newline: rendered as 'Uninstall \| residue check' -- the table survives, which a raw interpolation would not.
     - a single-result report with an empty outstanding list: scalar handled, '_Nothing recorded._' printed.
     - 1.2 MB report: truncated at 900000 characters with an explicit notice pointing at the artifact, final summary 900689 bytes, under GitHub's 1 MiB cap.
  3. A DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED BY RUNNING IT. ConvertFrom-Json turns the harness's ISO-8601 producedAt into a [datetime], and interpolating that rendered '10/02/2026 17:01:23' in the runner's locale -- ambiguous between two continents, timezone gone. The publisher now converts back to round-trip form. Inspection would not have found this.
  4. THE RESIDUE CLASSIFIER ON DELIBERATELY MESSY INPUT, which is the hazard section 6 of coordination/WINDOWS_LIFECYCLE_WIRING.md names. Given a service literally named 'LibertyBroadcast' at C:\\Vendor\\liberty-broadcast.exe, a Google updater scheduled task and the runner's own hostedtoolcache node.exe, classifyResidue returned clean with zero violations -- it matched on install-root containment and the product's registered names, and did not accuse the runner's software. Still only a fixture; the real service and process lists are what the first run is for.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No Windows machine has run any of this. msiexec, Get-CimInstance, Get-ScheduledTask and Get-Process were not executed anywhere; the harness refuses off win32 and that refusal was not circumvented. Whether the lifecycle harness passes on a runner is unknown and is precisely what the non-blocking step is for.

recommended.title: Install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall — tested, not assumed
recommended.acceptance: The installer's lifecycle is exercised automatically wherever that is possible on a runner, and everything that is not is named for the commander's machine. REQUIRED: clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch. REQUIRED: upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved, which is the one a release breaks most often and nobody tests. REQUIRED: uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps or removes. REQUIRED: reinstall after uninstall. REQUIRED: each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason, so the split is visible rather than implied.

review.evidence: CHANGES REQUESTED at 835823561c69f5bbdebf19c637eeeabff19dacf7. Transcribed by claude-lead from gpt-architect's round-105 ruling, section 2, which is a request for changes in substance even though it does not use the word: 'The lifecycle harness architecture is accepted. DO NOT mark PW-0503 DONE merely to free the Test lane. Current Windows evidence establishes only part of the lifecycle matrix.' gpt's itemised verdict: F1 clean install PARTIAL PASS -- the MSI builds, installs and its installed tree is verified; still unverified is actual installed application launch and WebView runtime. F2 upgrade UNVERIFIED -- no real previous release has been exercised as an upgrade source, so user-data preservation across an actual upgrade remains unproven. F3 uninstall PARTIAL PASS -- msiexec uninstall executes; still to prove where automation permits are no orphaned service, no scheduled task, no orphaned node.exe, expected files removed, and documented user-data retention behaviour. F4 reinstall UNVERIFIED but AUTOMATABLE -- 'implement and execute this rather than classifying it as commander-only'. WHAT HAS CHANGED SINCE THAT VERDICT WAS WRITTEN, and it narrows the request rather than answering it: the IMPLEMENTATION of F3's residue classification and of F4 reinstall already exists in scripts/windows/lifecycle.mjs and residue.mjs at the commit above, with 30 cases behind the decisions, and F4 is already marked plannedAutomated with no manual portion. What does not exist is EXECUTION, and it cannot be created by any open task: no open task can write .github/workflows/windows.yml -- every writer is DONE and PW-0502, PW-0503 and PW-0602 hold it read-only. That is recorded as a board.sequencing_finding and needs a ruling on which task gets the write surface. Recorded so the task leaves REVIEW honestly rather than being completed on evidence gpt declined to accept.
